record.title: CS/CS/HB 527 (2026): Mandatory Human Reviews of Insurance Claim Denials

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the Florida Senate bill page for HB 527 (2026) and the House Insurance & Banking Subcommittee (11 Dec 2025) and Commerce Committee (2 Mar 2026) bill analyses, stored from flsenate.gov on 14 Oct 2026 and found unchanged by the archiver on 17 Oct 2026. The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, versions (filed 24 Nov 2025, c1 posted 11 Dec 2025, c2 posted 27 Feb 2026), the 108-0 House vote of 5 Mar 2026 and 'Died in Rules' in the Senate on 13 Mar 2026; the Commerce analysis covers CS/CS/HB 527, the version the House passed, and the summary rests on it. The bill text itself was not stored.

title.quote: CS/CS/HB 527: Mandatory Human Reviews of Insurance Claim Denials

issuing_body.quote: Commerce Committee; Insurance & Banking Subcommittee; Cassel; (CO-INTRODUCERS)

official_identifier.quote: CS/CS/HB 527: Mandatory Human Reviews of Insurance Claim Denials

status.quote: Last Action: 3/13/2026 Senate - Died in Rules

legal_force.quote: Last Action: 3/13/2026 Senate - Died in Rules

summary.quote: It allows the use of these systems to assist in processing claims, but the bill prohibits the use of these systems as the sole basis to reduce a claim payment, deny a claim, or deny a portion of a claim.
analyze the claim independently of any AI system or machine learning system;
review the accuracy of any output produced by an AI system or machine learning system;
an affirmation that an AI system or machine learning system was not the sole basis for the denial.
must update their claims handling manuals with details about how these systems are used by the insurer and how those processes comply with the bill’s requirements.

notes.quote: Expanded the scope of the bill to include workers’ compensation and health maintenance organizations (HMOs).
Removed the definition of, and references to, “algorithm.”
Last Action: 3/13/2026 S Died in Banking and Insurance
The bill provides an effective date of July 1, 2026. (Section 4).

changes.title: removed the parenthetical '(passed House, died in Senate)': it records the bill's fate, which is in status and notes, and is not part of the bill's title on the Senate bill page

judgment.status_reasoning: The House passed CS/CS/HB 527 108-0 on 5 Mar 2026; in the Senate it was referred to Rules and the bill page's last action is 'Died in Rules' on 13 Mar 2026, the end of the 2026 Regular Session. A bill that died stays legal_force 'Proposed' with status 'Lapsed' (AGENTS.md section 5.6). Nothing stored shows a later enactment.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific bill on human review of insurance claim decisions made with AI and machine learning systems; a pending or lapsed AI bill is in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the filing date, 24 Nov 2025 (Bill Text table: 'H 527 Filed 11/24/2025'); date_last_updated is the posting of the last version, c2, on 27 Feb 2026, the text the House passed.
judgment.summary_reasoning: The current summary matches the Commerce Committee analysis of CS/CS/HB 527 (sections 1 to 3): assistive use allowed, no reduction or denial based solely on AI or ML output, the qualified human professional's three duties, records, the denial-letter affirmation and the claims-handling manual. Left unchanged.
